blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Eluviation is the washing out and leaching of soluble minerals and organic matter from upper soil horizons.
Illuviation is the process of deposition and accumulation of leached minerals in lower horizons (B horizon).
Podzolization occurs in cool, humid climates under coniferous vegetation, producing acidic, ash-grey soils.
Laterization involves heavy leaching of silica in hot, humid tropical climates, leaving behind iron and aluminum oxides.
Gleization occurs in poorly drained, waterlogged conditions, producing bluish-grey soils due to reduced iron compounds.

blocks.content: Soil forming processes continuously transform parent material through physical, chemical, and biological actions to develop distinct soil horizons.

rows: Leaching of Fe & Al oxides; silica remains
Leaching of silica; Fe & Al accumulate
Reduction of ferric iron to ferrous iron

items: Distinguish between Eluviation (removal/washing out from A horizon) and Illuviation (accumulation in B horizon).
Remember that Laterization removes silica and retains Fe/Al oxides, whereas Podzolization removes Fe/Al and retains silica.
Gleization is specifically tested in context with waterlogged, anaerobic conditions resulting in reduced ferrous iron.
